paper.title_en: Q-ESVC: Quantum Machine Learning Model for COVID-19 Like Disease Detection Using C-Xray Images
paper.abstract_en: Computerized diagnosis has become necessary for the fast and reliable detection of COVID-19 owing to its high transmission rate. By assisting in the containment of COVID-19 during the pandemic, automating the diagnosis procedure will reduce strain on the current healthcare system. Compared to other imaging and detection methods, chest X-ray (CXR) imaging offers several advantages. Although numerous studies have utilized chest X-ray datasets for COVID-19 diagnosis, limited attention has been given to combining image enhancement strategies with quantum-inspired machine-learning techniques. In this work, a novel quantum-inspired diagnostic model is developed for the identification of COVID-19 cases from CXR images. The framework leverages quantum computing principles, such as superposition, entanglement, and interference, alongside established machine-learning methodologies to improve classification effectiveness and computational performance. The proposed model Q-ESVC (Quantum-Enhanced Support Vector Classifier) is assessed against classifiers: the conventional SVM and the QSVC. Q-ESVC model outclassed the existing benchmarks in terms of Accuracy (99.78%), Precision (99.23%), and Recall (99.82%) and F1 score (94.47%), thereby demonstrating superior performance compared to its classical and quantum counterparts.
